name: The Seven Churches of Asia Minor
path: New Testament Studies: Life and Doctrine in Christ

objectives.text: Identify that the risen Jesus told John to write letters to seven churches
Describe John's vision of Jesus standing among seven golden lampstands and holding seven stars
Recall that Jesus tells each church that he knows their works
Name the seven churches of Asia Minor in the order Jesus addresses them
Identify the warning and the promise Jesus gives in a single letter such as the letter to Smyrna
Describe the common pattern of the letters including the title of Christ, commendation, rebuke, call to repent, call to hear, and promise to the one who conquers
Explain what Jesus means by calling the church in Laodicea lukewarm in light of its claim to be rich and in need of nothing
Explain the rebuke to Ephesus for abandoning its first love and the threefold remedy to remember, repent, and do the works it did at first
Compare the church in Smyrna, which was poor and suffering yet called rich, with the church in Sardis, which had a reputation for being alive yet was called dead
Locate the seven cities on a map of the Roman province of Asia and trace the route a messenger would travel to deliver the letters
Explain how Revelation interprets the stars as the angels of the churches and the lampstands as the churches themselves
Analyze how the title of Christ that opens each letter draws on the vision of chapter one and fits the needs of that church
Analyze how historical details of the cities such as emperor worship in Pergamum and the wealth and lukewarm water of Laodicea illuminate the letters
Identify the false teachings and compromises the letters name, including the Nicolaitans, the teaching of Balaam, and the woman Jezebel, and explain the danger each posed
Interpret the promises to the one who conquers and trace how several of them are fulfilled in the closing chapters of Revelation
Explain why the repeated call to hear what the Spirit says to the churches shows that the letters address the whole church in every age
Compare Ephesus, which guarded sound doctrine but lost its love, with Pergamum and Thyatira, which showed love and service but tolerated false teaching
Analyze the meaning of Jesus standing at the door and knocking when the verse is read in its context as a call to the church in Laodicea
Analyze how Christ's calls to repent and his warning to remove a church's lampstand relate to the Reformed teaching on church discipline and the marks of a true church
Explain how the call to Smyrna to be faithful unto death and the promise to keep Philadelphia relate to the Reformed doctrine of the perseverance of the saints
Evaluate how Christ holding the stars and walking among the lampstands supports the Reformed confession that Christ alone is head of the church
Evaluate how the warnings to the seven churches apply to congregations today by drawing principles from the original context rather than reading modern situations into the text
Evaluate major interpretive approaches to the seven churches, including letters to historical congregations, successive ages of church history, and timeless types, using evidence from the text
Create a study guide that examines a congregation using the categories the letters themselves use, such as works, love, doctrinal faithfulness, holiness, and endurance

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (seven letters, Jesus among lampstands, Jesus knows works, warnings and promises, letter pattern, Laodicea lukewarm, Smyrna and Sardis comparison, Ephesus first love, historical context, conqueror promises, universal application, lampstand meaning, health check, present relevance, authority of Christ, perseverance). Turned the vague 'observe' and 'synthesize' items into observable tasks tied to specific letters and to the Reformed doctrine of perseverance. Reframed the spiritual health check as a congregational study guide built on the letters' own categories so it assesses knowledge and skill, not inner experience. Added naming the seven cities, mapping the route, titles of Christ drawn from chapter one, the false teachings named in the letters, the truth and love contrast among Ephesus, Pergamum and Thyatira, Revelation 3:20 in context, church discipline and the marks of the church, and evaluation of interpretive approaches. Added verse-level references and confession anchors only where they state the doctrine taught, and left wider symbolism and the New Jerusalem to sibling sub-topics.
